lecture_title: Conformal Maps and the Open-String Scattering Prescription

assets.name: lecture_08_figure_01.png
assets.rationale: Shows the completed two-dimensional Poisson equation and expanded Laplacian before the wave-equation comparison.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: the second derivative with respect to x plus the second derivative with respect to y

assets.name: lecture_08_figure_02.png
assets.rationale: Captures the complete Cauchy--Riemann pair with the relative minus sign after both directional derivatives are compared.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: those are called the Cauchy Riemann equations

assets.name: lecture_08_figure_03.png
assets.rationale: Shows the mixed-derivative cancellation that leaves Laplace's equation for a component of an analytic map.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: the first two terms cancel and so you get zero

assets.name: lecture_08_figure_04.png
assets.rationale: Captures the completed ratio argument used to prove that analytic maps preserve relative angles.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: the angle between the two directions is the same

assets.name: lecture_08_figure_05.png
assets.rationale: Shows the full expansion of w=z squared and the resulting real and imaginary components.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: u is x squared minus y squared and v is two x y

assets.name: lecture_08_figure_06.png
assets.rationale: Shows complex conjugation as the clean counterexample that fails the Cauchy--Riemann equations.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: this is not an analytic function

assets.name: lecture_08_figure_07.png
assets.rationale: Shows the real and imaginary components of the complex exponential after Euler's formula is applied.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: e to the x times cosine y plus i sine y

assets.name: lecture_08_figure_08.png
assets.rationale: Captures the half-plane-to-strip logarithm map with rays and semicircles becoming an orthogonal rectangular grid.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: the half plane maps into an infinite strip

assets.name: lecture_08_figure_09.png
assets.rationale: Shows the half-plane and full-plane identifications that distinguish open-string strips from closed-string cylinders.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: the full plane is mapped into a cylinder

assets.name: lecture_08_figure_10.png
assets.rationale: Shows the linear-fractional map and the unit-circle boundary during the live interior/exterior convention discussion.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: the imaginary axis gets mapped into the unit circle

assets.name: lecture_08_figure_11.png
assets.rationale: Captures the completed circle-and-line grid inside the disc after the correspondence with half-plane rays and semicircles is explained.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: circles map into circles and lines map into circles or lines
assets.caption_hint: Orthogonal circle families in the disc

assets.name: lecture_08_figure_12.png
assets.rationale: Shows the completed positive Euclidean worldsheet action after the live sign correction is finished.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: both terms are positive in the Euclidean version

assets.name: lecture_08_figure_13.png
assets.rationale: Shows the slit-strip scattering worldsheet and its disc representation with four boundary points.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: this whole band-aid can be mapped into a disk
assets.caption_hint: Four-string strip mapped to a disc

assets.name: lecture_08_figure_14.png
assets.rationale: Shows the Euclidean bulk weight and the first boundary momentum insertion as separate factors.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: at this point you put e to the i k dot x

assets.name: lecture_08_figure_15.png
assets.rationale: Captures the complete board-level product of external momentum factors within the worldsheet path integral.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: the product of all these factors goes inside the path integral

assets.name: lecture_08_figure_16.png
assets.rationale: Shows the disc with boundary insertions while momentum components are interpreted as independent electrostatic charges.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: twenty-six different kinds of charge at each point

assets.name: lecture_08_figure_17.png
assets.rationale: Shows four boundary insertions after conformal freedom has fixed three positions, leaving one modulus.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: only the location of the fourth point gets integrated
